title: COPAS Wormsorter Protocol
author: Saul Moore
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.bfc9jiz6
materials: Open FlowPilot software and a prepared experiment with a set gate for eg Adults. :
Select number of objects to sort
Turn off all equipment (Computer, lasers, compressor, worm sorter).

steps.title: Power on compressor
steps.instruction: Turn on the wall‑mounted compressor; verify the pressure gauge reads 40 psi before proceeding.

steps.title: Power on COPAS instrument
steps.instruction: Switch on the COPAS wormsorter using the power switch on the left side of the machine.

steps.title: Activate lasers and computer
steps.instruction: Turn on the computer and the lasers (activate the 488 nm laser; the 568 nm laser may also be turned on if required).

steps.title: Empty recovery cup
steps.instruction: Discard any waste liquid that is present in the recovery cup (the small shallow cup on the left‑hand side of the machine).

steps.title: Check sheath water level
steps.instruction: Inspect the sheath water line; if the water level is low, fill it with MQ H₂O (do NOT use M9 buffer).

steps.title: Secure cups to prevent leaks
steps.instruction: Make sure both the recovery cup and the sample cup are tightly screwed in so that no leaks are present in the system.

steps.title: Refill sample cup
steps.instruction: In the COPAS software, click ‘Refill Sample’; the sample‑cup pressure should decrease (visible on the left side of the software). If the pressure rises, a blockage may be present.

steps.title: Load cleaning solution
steps.instruction: Unscrew the sample cup and replace it with a Falcon tube filled with pink cleaning solution.

steps.title: Run cleaning solution through system
steps.instruction: Check ‘Sample on’ and ‘Mixer on’; allow 2–3 ml of cleaning solution to pass (ensure the sheath is unchecked). A warning about contaminating the flow cell will appear—click ‘Yes’ to continue.

substeps.instruction: Verify that cleaning solution is flowing.
Allow 2–3 ml to pass before proceeding.

steps.title: Stop sample flow
steps.instruction: Uncheck ‘Sample on’ or click ‘Abort’ to halt the sample flow.

steps.title: Flush system with water
steps.instruction: Repeat the actions of steps 8–10 using a Falcon tube filled with MQ H₂O instead of cleaning solution.

steps.title: Load experimental sample
steps.instruction: Repeat the actions of steps 8–10 with the actual worm sample in the sample cup.

steps.title: Turn mixer on
steps.instruction: Activate the mixer; failure to do so may cause worms to settle at the bottom of the tube and be lost.

steps.title: Prime flow cell
steps.instruction: From the Maintenance menu, select ‘Prime Flow Cell’ to flush the sample through the system and remove any air bubbles.

steps.title: Verify laser boxes
steps.instruction: Check that the 488 nm (and, if used, the 568 nm) laser boxes are turned on.

steps.title: Enable stored sort gate
steps.instruction: In the software, check ‘Use sort gate’ to load the previously stored sort gate.

steps.title: Acquire sample and set event rate
steps.instruction: Click ‘Acquire’; the sample should flow and the events‑per‑second readout will appear. Aim for 10–20 events s⁻¹. Adjust the sample‑cup pressure to 1.5–2 psi if the rate is too low or high, and select ‘Pure, no double’ under Setup → Coincidence to ensure one event per droplet.

steps.title: Prepare 60 mm plate
steps.instruction: Click the plate icon on the top bar, select a spare 60 mm plate, choose wells A1, A2, B1, B2, and click ‘Apply’. Place the plate in the front‑left corner of the left‑hand stage with well A1 at the left corner.

steps.title: Fill 60 mm plate
steps.instruction: Click ‘Fill plate’ while monitoring the events‑per‑second readout and confirming that ‘Diverter pressure’ is checked.

steps.title: Verify dispensing under microscope
steps.instruction: Inspect the plate under a microscope to confirm the correct number of objects were dispensed per well. If too many objects were delivered, decrease the sample‑cup pressure and repeat steps 8–11 or enable ‘Pure, no double’ and repeat.

steps.title: Prepare 96‑well plate
steps.instruction: Click the plate icon again, select the desired number of objects per well, click ‘Apply to All’ (or set per‑well values), and place the 96‑well plate on the left‑hand stage. Ensure ‘Diverter pressure’ is checked to avoid constant liquid flow.

steps.title: Run sorting on 96‑well plate
steps.instruction: Start the sort, keep an eye on the events‑per‑second readout and the amount of sample fluid flowing through the system.

steps.title: Secure sample cup for airtight system
steps.instruction: Keep the sample cup filled with water securely tightened so that the system remains airtight and closed after sorting.

description: Open dbgview – should always be running in the background
